evidence.reason: The finding asks to add hold-ownership rechecks (and to serialize marker changes) at the two `helper.switch` boundaries. That is a proposal to enlarge protection scope/harden a race, not an implementation error in existing intended behavior. The code deliberately acquires the marker once (line 772-773) and holds it across stop/drain/switch; the explicit `hold.owns()` guards at stop (line 809) and before the rollback drain are the chosen checkpoints. The alleged harm (switching while the runner is active after an operator removes the marker mid-drain) is already mitigated by the helper's own unit-inactivity check as the finding itself notes, and losing the marker requires out-of-band operator editing outside the supported transaction model. No supplied contract clause, test, or API semantics requires a pre-switch owner recheck, and serializing marker changes with the switch is a substantial architectural change needing owner direction rather than a routine correctness repair. Contract points ownership rules to linked docs, but contract silence does not itself establish this obligation.
